Nurses should be presented with treatment recommendations that describe the validity and confidence of prediction and shown the chain of logic that rests the final decision for the appropriate course of treatment with nurses.
It is also apparent that a detailed description of the functions of decision logic is required to support the implementation of AI-based interventions.

Tools that utilise glass-box design, such as InterpretML ( Nori et al., 2019 ), which allow the developer and researcher to understand the model’s inner workings, should be encouraged and incorporated into clinical interfaces.

unlisted_practices: Describe AI interventions in terms of competence, reliability and validity, as expected of other clinical tools where quality and safety are a priority.
Nursing leadership bodies should develop AI strategies to ensure nursing has a clear direction and voice in AI-driven change.
Nurses should partner with developers and researchers to influence the conversation about AI and direct its power towards improving outcomes.
Apply design thinking and empathy-focused methods, including end users and clinicians, when designing and developing AI interventions.
Frame future research to better understand how AI is used to deliver care and how it affects people with mental illness.
Appraise AI clinical decision support tools within an evidence-based decision-making framework rather than relying on trust alone.
Accelerate training of the health workforce in AI by developing foundational AI frameworks for health professionals and accredited programmes.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual commentary/perspective paper discussing the framework of trust versus reliability and validity for AI implementation in nursing.
